blocks.heading: Informative and persuasive advertising
blocks.text: Informative advertising emphasises facts about the offering, such as features, price, location or how to use it. Persuasive advertising emphasises reasons to prefer or want it, often through a benefit or identity. A message can contain both. Classify by emphasis rather than assuming all information is neutral or all persuasion gives no facts. Neither purpose permits inaccurate claims. The right balance depends on what the target needs to know and why it might choose the offer.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: One bag advert lists capacity, price and collection point; another stresses the confidence of keeping tools organised. The first mainly informs; the second mainly persuades through a benefit. The persuasive message still needs to reflect what the bag can actually do.

blocks.heading: Informative advertising
blocks.text: Informative advertising emphasises full relevant information about the product or service. It can explain features, uses, price, availability or a new arrangement, helping customers make sense of an unfamiliar offer. Accurate facts still need a clear audience and accessible presentation. Informative and persuasive elements can coexist in one advert.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A meal notice states the menu, price, collection point and time. Its main emphasis supplies practical facts rather than a lifestyle appeal. Those facts still need to be accurate and useful.

blocks.heading: Persuasive advertising
blocks.text: Persuasive advertising emphasises reasons to prefer or want an offering. It may highlight a benefit, emotion or identity to build preference over rivals. It can contain factual information as well, and persuasion should remain consistent with the actual product. A striking message without a credible benefit may attract attention but fail to convert interest into a purchase.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A bag advert stresses keeping tools organised and ready for work. That benefit-led appeal is persuasive. The bag still needs compartments that support the claimed usefulness.
